newsitem.title: UK: UK electric, water stocks to weather utility tax.
newsitem.headline: UK electric, water stocks to weather utility tax.

text.p: The tax on privatised utilities announced by the new Labour government on Wednesday is in line with expectations and should not hurt water and electricity sector shares when markets open on Thursday, analysts said on Wednesday.

"It's much in line, it's one-off which is good news, payment over two years is also helpful...I don't suppose there's going to be too much lack of sleep tonight," said Marshall Whiting, analyst at SGST, said.
Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown announced that he planned to raise a total 5.2 billion stg from the tax, only slightly ahead of market expectations of five billion stg.
He said 2.1 billion stg of that would come from the electricity sector, around 1.65 billion stg from water firms and 1.45 billion stg from others.

The tax will cover companies privatised by flotation and regulated by statute and includes water and electricity companies as well as British Telecom, BAA, British Gas, now BG Plc and Centrica, and Railtrack.
Brown "has gone for a basis which is designed to give certainty...which I think the markets should welcome," said Richard Savours of Coopers & Lybrand.
The formula to calculate the tax looks at the difference between valuation at the time of flotation and net profits in the four years since then.
